props.title: The War Game
props.initialSlug: Chilling mockumentary of nuclear war's British aftermath

sections.content: The War Game represents a seismic shift in nuclear war cinema, delivering a devastating pseudo-documentary that proved so shocking the BBC banned it from television for 20 years. Director Peter Watkins pioneered a documentary-style approach to speculative fiction that influenced films like Threads (1984) and Special Bulletin (1983). Shot in stark black and white with non-professional actors, Watkins meticulously depicts a nuclear attack on Britain with unflinching medical accuracy and social commentary that still terrifies viewers today.

sections.content: The film sparked a wave of nuclear apocalypse cinema that peaked in the 1980s with works like The Day After (1983) and When the Wind Blows (1986). These films shared Watkins' commitment to scientific accuracy but reached mainstream audiences through network television and animation respectively. The documentary approach pioneered in The War Game influenced later works like Countdown to Looking Glass (1984) and By Dawn's Early Light (1990), which used news footage formatting to create verisimilitude.

Watkins' innovative mixing of documentary and dramatic techniques created a new subgenre of speculative documentary that extends beyond nuclear themes. Films like District 9 (2009) and What We Left Behind (2019) employ similar strategies to explore social issues through a science fiction lens. The War Game's unflinching examination of institutional failure during crisis particularly resonates with modern disaster films like Contagion (2011). SUBHEAD: Impact on Political Documentary

movies.title: Threads
movies.slug: Brutally realistic BBC film following nuclear war's immediate and long-term effects on Sheffield, England

sections.content: The film's influence extends into pure documentary, inspiring filmmakers to incorporate dramatic recreations and speculative scenarios. Errol Morris's The Thin Blue Line (1988) and Peter Davis's Hearts and Minds (1974) both show traces of Watkins' technique. The War Game's focus on interviewing ordinary citizens about extraordinary circumstances became a template for crisis documentaries like The Atomic Cafe (1982) and Radio Bikini (1988).
